default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-158.title: Risk-incoherent index move fade
E-158.hypothesis: WIN and WDO normally move against each other because foreign flow buys the index and sells the dollar together; when both rise (or fall) clearly over the same window, the index move has no foreign flow behind it, only local traders, and the dealers who absorbed it lean it back; fade the index move.

E-159.title: Session-midpoint first-touch hold
E-159.hypothesis: On a day with a wide range, the midpoint of the session's high-low is the line day traders use to call the day bullish or bearish; after price has traded only in the upper half for a while, the first touch of the midpoint that closes back above meets the buyers defending the day's bias; trade away from it.

E-160.title: Hour-end painting fade
E-160.hypothesis: When the last minutes of a clock hour print the hour's high and the hour closes on it, short-term traders pushed the hourly candle's close (cosmetic marking for hourly charts and alerts) rather than new information; once the new hour starts the pushers stop and the price gives the mark back; fade it.

E-161.title: Participation turn follow
E-161.hypothesis: When the volume of the last window crosses well above its normal level for that time of day while price has moved, new participants are entering on one side (an information or rebalancing event starting), and that flow is split over the following bars; follow the window's direction at the turn.

E-162.title: Wide indecision bar break follow
E-162.hypothesis: A bar much wider than normal that closes in its middle third ran the stops on both sides and left both camps trapped near its extremes; the first close beyond its high (low) within a few bars shows which side gave up, and its exits plus the new entries push the price on; follow the break.

E-163.title: Volatile-dollar index break follow
E-163.hypothesis: When the dollar is trading a range far above normal, macro and foreign desks are repositioning across Brazilian assets; index breaks of the recent high/low in that regime carry macro order flow rather than local noise, so they extend; follow WIN breaks only while the dollar is volatile.

E-164.title: Macro-backed dip buy
E-164.hypothesis: A falling dollar over the last hour signals foreign money coming into Brazil, which keeps bidding for the index; a short-term index dip to a new 15-minute low in that regime is local selling the foreign flow absorbs, so the first bar closing above the previous bar's high is bought (mirror with a rising dollar).

E-165.title: Round-trip rejection follow
E-165.hypothesis: When price runs far from where it stood a window ago and then closes back below that starting price, the whole excursion was rejected: everyone who bought the run is under water and the responsive sellers have proven the higher prices unacceptable, so the return keeps going; follow the completed round trip.

E-166.title: Dollar-high rejection buys the index
E-166.hypothesis: A new short-term dollar high that is knocked back sharply in the next bar shows FX dealers selling the dollar spike (foreign inflow or central-bank-sensitive supply); the index, priced off the same foreign flow, moves the other way with a lag, so buy WIN on the dollar rejection (mirror at a dollar low).

E-167.title: Fizzled day-move follow-through
E-167.hypothesis: A move from the open that reached well beyond the usual distance for the time of day and has now fallen back near the open within the hour has failed: the trend-day buyers are trapped above and their exits push price further back; follow the fizzle in the direction of the retreat.
